title: A Festive Foodie Christmas in Hong Kong: 6 days of dim sum, harbour lights & holiday magic for two
description: Hong Kong at Christmas is pure sensory magic — neon-lit skyscrapers draped in festive lights, harbour breezes carrying the scent of sizzling street food, and mild winter weather perfect for exploring on foot. This itinerary weaves Michelin-starred dim sum with legendary street food crawls, spa relaxation with breathtaking peaks, and the festive glow of WinterFest with the timeless charm of fishing villages and ancient temples. It's Asia's most dazzling holiday destination.

days.title: Arrival & Christmas Lights on the Harbour
days.description: Touch down and dive straight into Hong Kong's festive energy. Settle into Kowloon, indulge in iconic afternoon tea, then watch the harbour skyline transform into a Christmas light show.

activities.name: Arrive & Get Your Octopus Card
activities.description: Clear customs and grab an Octopus card at the airport kiosk. Take the Airport Express to Kowloon Station (24 min) — fast, smooth, and scenic as you approach the skyline. Drop bags at your hotel in Tsim Sha Tsui, then head to The Peninsula lobby for Hong Kong's most legendary afternoon tea — scones, finger sandwiches, and pastries served under gilded columns with a live string quartet.

activities.name: Tsim Sha Tsui Promenade & Christmas Walk
activities.description: Walk along the Avenue of Stars as the harbour skyline transitions from golden hour to a sea of festive lights. During WinterFest, the East TST buildings along Mody Road glow with snowflake projections and LED video walls.

days.neighborhoods: Sham Shui Po · Sheung Wan · Central · Victoria Peak
days.title: Christmas Eve — Dim Sum, Temples & Peak Sunset
days.description: From the world's cheapest Michelin star to a sunset over 7 million twinkling lights — Christmas Eve in Hong Kong is a day of contrasts. Street-level soul food, ancient temples, and sky-high elegance.

activities.name: Sheung Wan & Man Mo Temple
activities.description: Wander antique shops and galleries along Hollywood Road, then step into Man Mo Temple (built 1847). Giant incense coils hang from the ceiling, filling the space with fragrant smoke — mesmerizing and photogenic. Grab beef brisket noodles at century-old Kau Kee (cash only, worth the queue), then ride the world's longest outdoor covered escalator through SoHo — a moving window into Hong Kong's vertical neighbourhoods.

activities.name: Victoria Peak Sunset via Peak Tram
activities.description: Take the historic Peak Tram up to Victoria Peak and arrive before sunset to watch the city transform from daylight to a sea of lights. Skip the mall — walk the free Lugard Road trail for the best panoramic vantage points.

days.neighborhoods: Tsim Sha Tsui · Central · Mong Kok · Jordan
days.title: Christmas Day — Harbour, Markets & Sky-High Cocktails
days.description: Christmas in Hong Kong is vibrant, not quiet. Start with a lavish brunch, cruise the harbour on the Star Ferry, explore the festive installations, then dive into Kowloon's electric night markets before drinks at the highest bar in the world.

activities.name: Star Ferry & Harbour City Christmas
activities.description: Take the iconic green-and-white Star Ferry from TST to Central (HK$3.70 — the city's best bargain). Sit on the lower deck for open-air harbour breezes. Then loop back to Harbour City for massive outdoor Christmas installations and photo ops. Dive into Kowloon's most intense neighbourhood — Ladies' Market on Tung Choi Street, the Goldfish Market, and the Flower Market. Haggle for souvenirs, soak in the neon-lit chaos, and feel the pulse of local Hong Kong.

activities.name: Temple Street Night Market
activities.description: As dusk falls, Temple Street comes alive with dai pai dong (open-air food stalls). Try clay pot rice, typhoon shelter crab, and stinky tofu. Fortune tellers and Cantonese opera singers add to the atmosphere.

days.neighborhoods: Jordan · Lantau Island · Ngong Ping · Tai O
days.title: Lantau Island — Big Buddha, Cable Car & Fishing Village
days.description: Escape the urban buzz for a day of mountain air, ancient monasteries, and a fishing village frozen in time. The Ngong Ping cable car ride alone is worth the trip.

activities.name: Ngong Ping 360 Crystal Cabin
activities.description: Take the MTR to Tung Chung, then board the Ngong Ping 360 cable car. Upgrade to the Crystal Cabin with its glass-bottom floor for vertigo-inducing views over the South China Sea, airport, and lush mountains.

activities.name: Tian Tan Buddha (Big Buddha)
activities.description: Climb the 268 steps to the 34-metre bronze Buddha for panoramic views over Lantau. The adjacent Po Lin Monastery is serene and beautiful. Buy a meal ticket at the base for the monastery's vegetarian lunch.

activities.name: Tai O Fishing Village
activities.description: Take bus #21 from Ngong Ping to Tai O — Hong Kong's last stilt-house fishing village. Wander narrow lanes past traditional pang uk houses over the water, spot pink dolphins on a boat tour (HK$25), and sample dried seafood snacks.

days.neighborhoods: Tsim Sha Tsui · Wan Chai · Central
days.title: Spa Day, Star Street & Farewell Feast
days.description: The relaxation day you've earned. Morning couples spa, playful dim sum, a leafy neighbourhood stroll, then one of the greatest Cantonese meals on Earth.

activities.name: Couples Spa at The Peninsula
activities.description: Treat yourselves to a 90-minute couples massage at The Peninsula Spa. The signature Peninsula Wellness Journey combines aromatherapy, deep tissue, and hot stones in a serene space above the city.

activities.name: Star Street Precinct & Wan Chai
activities.description: Cross to Hong Kong Island and explore the leafy Star Street area — independent coffee shops (try Cupping Room), wine bars, and galleries in a quiet pocket of sophistication. Then walk through the adjacent Wan Chai wet market for a dose of old Hong Kong.

days.neighborhoods: Yau Ma Tei · Mong Kok · Kowloon
days.title: Morning Stroll & Departure
days.description: A gentle farewell morning — vintage cha chaan teng breakfast, a peaceful park walk, and one last pineapple bun for the road.

activities.name: Kowloon Park Morning Walk
activities.description: A peaceful green oasis in TST — flamingos in the bird lake, sculpture gardens, and tai chi practitioners in the morning light. A calm, centering way to close out the trip.

activities.name: Airport Express to HKG
activities.description: Take the Airport Express from Kowloon Station — 24 minutes to the airport. In-town check-in lets you drop bags at the station and travel light. Allow 2.5 hours before your flight.
